@about: Lighting plot add-on (0.8 SU.766). Words of the add-on only.
cmd.lpos.help: Draw a lighting position (pipe, truss, boom or floor line) with a name
cmd.lfix.help: Place lighting fixtures, on a position or spread along it
cmd.lnum.help: Number the units along each position and, if you like, the channels
cmd.lset.help: Set channel, address, purpose, colour, wattage or note on selected fixtures (101+ numbers them in a row)
cmd.lsched.help: The instrument schedule: print it, or draw it as a table
cmd.lhook.help: The channel hookup: print it, or draw it as a table
cmd.llegend.help: Draw the legend: every fixture type in use, with its symbol, count and watts
ask.pos.name: Position name (for example 1E, FOH 2, Box boom SL)
ask.fix.aim: Aim in degrees (270 = down the page)
ask.num: Number units: start {start}, channels {chan}, reverse {reverse}, restart on each position {restart} [Go/Start/Channels/Reverse/Position restart]
ask.set.value.seq: Value, or 101+ to number the selection in a row (101+2 counts by 2)
ask.table.at: Top left of the table (Enter to only print it)
err.pos.name: A position needs a name.
err.pos.taken: There is a position named {name} already.
err.pos.points: A position needs at least two points (a boom, one).
err.nofix: There are no lighting fixtures in this drawing.
err.notpos: That is not a lighting position.
warn.loose: {n} fixtures are on no position and were not numbered.
done.export: EXPORT writes them as CSV or one workbook.
prob.dmx.overlap: {ta} at {a} and {tb} at {b} use the same DMX addresses.
prob.dimmer.over: Dimmer {addr} carries {watts} W; its limit is {max} W.
fix.link: Put them on the nearest position
set.tol: A fixture belongs to a position within (mm)
set.restart: Restart unit numbers on each position
cmd.lphoto.help: Give a fixture type its photometry file (.ies or .ldt) for the lux calculation (LPH)
cmd.llux.help: Direct illuminance on an area from the plot's fixtures, point by point; writes the values on the drawing (LUX)
photo.ask: Photometry for which fixture type? {list} [or Remove]
photo.which: Remove the file of which type? {list}
photo.removed: The photometry file of {type} was removed.
photo.big: That file is over {kb} KB, so it was not kept.
photo.bad: {name} could not be read as an IES or EULUMDAT file.
photo.nostore: This browser has no room to keep that file.
photo.set: {type} now uses {name}. It is kept in this browser.
lux.nolib: No fixture type has a photometry file yet. Use LPHOTO to give one.
lux.corner: First corner of the area to calculate (or Object to use a closed polyline)
lux.object: Pick a closed polyline round the area
lux.notclosed: That is not a closed polyline.
lux.flat: The area has no width or height.
lux.mount: Mounting height of the fixtures in millimetres (a fixture's own height wins)
lux.work: Height of the surface to calculate on, in millimetres (0 = the floor)
lux.spacing: Spacing of the calculation points in millimetres
lux.badfile: The photometry file of {type} could not be read, so its fixtures are left out.
lux.nofixture: No fixture has a readable photometry file, so there is nothing to calculate.
lux.toomany: That area at that spacing needs more than 40,000 points. Use a wider spacing.
lux.skipped: {n} fixtures have no photometry file and are left out.
lux.result: {n} fixtures, {points} points: lowest {min} lux, average {avg}, highest {max}; lowest over average {uni}.
lux.lpd: {lumens} lm and {watts} W over {area} m², {lpd} W/m².
